dimension: External I/O cost — outbound integrations (email/Resend, SMTP, TextSMS, M-Pesa/Daraja, Sentry, pg_net)
summary: External I/O is dominated by one pathology: a self-feeding email retry loop. The platform has made ~47,900 outbound email provider calls in its lifetime to deliver 705 messages (68:1 waste), and is currently burning ~1,200 outbound email calls/day — 100% of its Resend daily quota — re-sending one broken verification email to one real person. The SMTP fallback beneath it has a perfect 0-for-23,548 record and blocks ~30s per attempt inside the cron invocation, which is why `email_retry_failed` has never once completed. By contrast the SMS/TextSMS path is genuinely healthy (proper backoff, dispatch-log dedup, chunked bulk sends, and DLR polling already cut from 19,127 lifetime provider calls to 331 by the shipped back-off) — the standing "replace DLR polling with a webhook" item would now save nothing. Secondary but real: the job-queue dedup index frees on completion, so every scheduled job runs 2–12× per window (16 extra Daraja Account Balance calls per 7 days); the pg_cron→/api/cron trigger times out on 100% of its 288 daily calls; and Sentry is ingesting ~490 events/day, all from three repeating cron conditions.

findings.title: retryFailedEmails is an unbounded self-feeding retry loop: ~1,200 outbound email calls/day to deliver ~200, and it re-sends with empty template vars
findings.evidence: lib/services/scheduler.service.ts:71-104. The header comment claims "fewer than 3 retries" but the SQL (lines 75-82) is `SELECT * FROM email_logs WHERE status='failed' AND created_at >= NOW()-'24 hours' AND created_at <= NOW()-'5 minutes' ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 50` — no retry counter, no exclusion of already-retried rows, and no column is ever written to mark one. Each retry calls sendTemplatedEmail (line 89) which INSERTs a NEW email_logs row; a failed retry is itself immediately eligible, so the population never shrinks. Line 92 passes `vars: {}`, so every retry renders with empty variables. Live prod: `SELECT provider,status,count(*) FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1,2` → resend failed 23,598 / sent 705 / queued 78; smtp failed 19,682 / queued 3,866 / sent 0. `SELECT date_trunc('day',created_at), count(*) FILTER (WHERE provider='resend'), count(*) FILTER (WHERE provider='smtp'), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status='sent') FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1` → 2026-09-04: 697 Resend calls + 499 SMTP calls, 196 sent; 2026-09-03: 726 + 526, 200 sent. `SELECT template_key,count(*),count(DISTINCT "to") FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1` → group_verification_link 44,963 rows to 2 distinct recipients (97% of all email ever attempted). In the last 2 days ezrawafula98@gmail.com received 557 status='sent' copies. pg_stat_statements: the retry SELECT has 28,002 calls / 1,050,480 ms total.
findings.impact: ~1,200 outbound provider calls/day for ≤200 deliveries; ~47,900 lifetime calls for 705 delivered messages (68:1). The ~200 deliveries/day are duplicate junk to one address, rendered with empty vars so the verification link is absent. 6,000 real sends/month pushes the account off Resend's free 3,000/mo tier onto Pro (~$20/mo ≈ KES 2,600/mo) purely for waste, and Gmail-side reputation damage from ~500 identical messages/day to one recipient is a live deliverability risk for the whole domain.
findings.recommendation: Add `retry_count`/`next_retry_at` columns to email_logs (mirror the sms_failures model that already works — lib/services/sms.service.ts:937-943 writes `next_retry_at = NOW() + INTERVAL '5 minutes'` with a retry_count/max_retries cap). Exclude rows whose error is permanent (unverified domain, quota exceeded) from retry entirely. Persist the original `vars` on the log row (or a payload table) so a retry re-renders the real email instead of an empty one; a retry that cannot reproduce its variables should not be sent at all. Until then, the cheapest correct stopgap is to disable the email_retry_failed job type.

findings.title: SMTP fallback has never succeeded once in 23,548 attempts and blocks ~30s per attempt because nodemailer is created with no timeouts
findings.evidence: lib/email/adapters/smtp.ts:6-16 — `nodemailer.createTransport({host, port, secure, auth})` with no `connectionTimeout`, `greetingTimeout`, `socketTimeout`, or `pool`, so nodemailer's 30,000 ms default greetingTimeout governs every failure. lib/email/provider.ts:71-74 fires this fallback on every primary failure whenever SMTP_HOST is set. Live prod: `SELECT provider,status,count(*) FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1,2` → provider='smtp' has 19,682 failed + 3,866 queued and **zero** 'sent' rows, ever (first attempt 2026-08-16 19:34). Dominant error: "Greeting never received" (19,675 rows); 5 rows read "connect ETIMEDOUT 102.212.247.131:465". The 3,866 'queued' rows are the INSERT-before-send at smtp.ts:28-46 that was never updated — i.e. the invocation was killed mid-sendMail. Timing proof from consecutive rows: resend row 00:50:13.246 → smtp row created 00:50:13.896 → next email's resend row 00:50:45.632, a 31.7s gap consistent with the 30s greeting timeout.
findings.impact: ~500 wasted outbound TCP/TLS connections per day to a host that has never accepted a message, each holding the serverless invocation for ~30s. This is the direct cause of the next finding (email_retry_failed never finishing) and therefore a first-order contributor to the job-queue starvation already banked. 3,866 invocations have been killed mid-send.
findings.recommendation: Either fix SMTP_HOST/credentials or remove SMTP from the fallback chain (unset SMTP_HOST). Regardless, set explicit `connectionTimeout: 5000, greetingTimeout: 5000, socketTimeout: 10000` and add a circuit breaker: after N consecutive failures with zero successes, stop attempting the fallback. A fallback with a 0% lifetime success rate must not be on the hot path of a time-budgeted cron tick.

findings.title: email_retry_failed has never completed a single job — it consumes a whole 60s Vercel invocation every 5 minutes and mints a new queue row each tick
findings.evidence: Live prod: `SELECT jl.status, left(jl.message,90), count(*) FROM job_logs jl JOIN job_queue jq ON jq.id=jl.job_id WHERE jq.type='email_retry_failed' AND jl.created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '3 days' GROUP BY 1,2` returns ONLY 'started' rows — 154 at attempt 1/5, 154 at 2/5, 154 at 3/5(153), 154 at 4/5, 153 at 5/5 = 768 starts, **zero** 'completed', 'retried' or 'failed' log rows. It starts, burns the tick on 2 emails × (1 Resend call + 1 blocking 30s SMTP call), is killed at the platform ceiling, is reset by resetStuckJobs after 6 min, and repeats until max_attempts. `SELECT type,status,count(*) FROM job_queue GROUP BY 1,2` → email_retry_failed: 4,612 pending, 917 failed, 4,200 completed, 2 processing. Its dedup key is time-bucketed (`email_retry_failed:${dateStr}T${hour}:${fiveMinBucket}`, lib/jobs/index.ts:67-70), unlike the four SMS sweeps that were converted to constant keys (lib/jobs/index.ts:81-131), so a new row is minted every 5 minutes whether or not the previous one ever ran. Tick budget is 50s inside a 60s ceiling (lib/jobs/processor.ts:72).
findings.impact: One of ~18 competing job types permanently consumes an entire cron invocation every 5 minutes while producing 2 junk emails, and grows the queue by 288 rows/day unboundedly. Sentry corroborates: "[jobs] 1 stuck job(s) exhausted max_attempts and were failed" fires roughly every 25 minutes. This is a named, fixable cause of the starvation the lead already measured, not a separate mystery.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same constant-dedup-key treatment already used for the SMS sweeps (lib/jobs/index.ts:81-131) to email_retry_failed, email_campaign_process, email_campaign_drain, mpesa_reconcile, mpesa_replay_callbacks and outbox_dispatch — the code comment at lib/jobs/index.ts:107-110 explicitly notes these were deliberately left out. Additionally make retryFailedEmails deadline-aware via lib/jobs/deadline.ts (tickBudgetExhausted), as pollPendingDlrs already does at sms.service.ts:1278, so it stops cleanly instead of being killed.

findings.title: Every scheduled job runs 2–12× per window: the dedup unique index excludes 'completed', so a fast daily job is re-enqueued on each remaining 5-minute tick of its hour
findings.evidence: Index: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_job_queue_dedup ON job_queue (dedup_key) WHERE dedup_key IS NOT NULL AND status <> ALL (ARRAY['completed','failed'])`. Daily blocks in lib/jobs/index.ts:184-353 are guarded only by `hour === N`, with no `fiveMinBucket === 0` guard (contrast the hourly block at line 151 which HAS one). So once the first copy completes, the key frees and the next tick enqueues another. Direct proof: `SELECT dedup_key,status,created_at FROM job_queue WHERE type='sms_birthday_reminders' AND created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '30 hours'` → SEVEN rows all keyed `sms_birthday_reminders:2026-09-04`, all 'completed', at 04:00, 04:05, 04:10, 04:15, 04:20, 04:25, 04:55 UTC. Control that falsifies the alternative explanation: payment_orphan_monitor (bucket-guarded) is exactly 24 rows/day. Full 7-day tally via `SELECT type, count(*), count(DISTINCT dedup_key), count(*)-count(DISTINCT dedup_key) FROM job_queue WHERE created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '7 days' AND dedup_key IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>count(DISTINCT dedup_key)`: sms_birthday_reminders 56 runs/7 intended, notify_loan_due_alerts 52/7, cleanup_expired_tokens 45/8, mpesa_reconcile_charges 36/8, mpesa_daily_report 31/7, email_recurring_invoices 31/7, email_birthday 24/7, mpesa_balance_snapshot 23/7, email_overdue_invoices 22/7, notify_contribution_reminders 10/1, governance_compute_metrics 5/1.
findings.impact: External-I/O cost: mpesa_balance_snapshot (lib/jobs/handlers.ts:272-278) issues a real Daraja Account Balance query per run — 16 unnecessary Safaricom API calls per 7 days. mpesa_daily_report runs 24 extra times/7d at 14.3s avg (344s of function time). notify_contribution_reminders — the exact job that produced the 2026-07-01 duplicate-SMS storm (192 sends where 16 were wanted, 96 provider-accepted duplicates, one member receiving the identical message 12 times) — still fires 10× per monthly window; the only thing preventing repeat billed SMS today is the downstream reminder_dispatch_log claim in sendOnce(). Job-level dedup is not actually protecting anything.
findings.recommendation: Wrap every daily/weekly/monthly block in lib/jobs/index.ts in `if (fiveMinBucket === 0)` as the hourly block already does — a one-line guard per block. Better still, change the dedup index to omit 'completed' from the exclusion for time-scoped keys (keep the constant-key sweeps working by giving them a distinct mechanism), so a daily key stays claimed for its whole day.

findings.title: 100% of pg_cron's outbound calls to /api/cron time out: timeout_milliseconds=20000 against a 50s tick budget
findings.evidence: `SELECT command FROM cron.job WHERE jobid=2` → net.http_post to 'https://kitabuyetu.vercel.app/api/cron' with `timeout_milliseconds := 20000`. lib/jobs/processor.ts:72 sets TIME_BUDGET_MS = 50_000 inside a 60s ceiling, so the handler cannot answer inside 20s by design. Live prod: `SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code IS NULL OR status_code>=400) FROM net._http_response` → 72 of 72 responses in the retained 6-hour window are non-2xx/NULL. Every row reads `timed_out=true`, `status_code=null`, e.g. "Timeout of 20000 ms reached. Total time: 20001.956000 ms (DNS time: 147.129 ms, TCP/SSL handshake 67.468 ms, HTTP Request/Response 19783.433 ms)". cron.job_run_details shows 288 'succeeded' pg_cron runs in 24h — pg_cron considers the enqueue a success, so the timeout is completely invisible from the scheduler's side.
findings.impact: 288 outbound HTTP calls/day (~96 minutes/day of pg_net worker wall time) that can never return a usable result. The DB has zero visibility into whether the cron endpoint 200s, 401s or 500s — a broken CRON_SECRET or a bad deploy would look identical to today. It also means the 2.6 hours of net._http_response cleanup exec time already banked is spent maintaining rows that carry no information at all.
findings.recommendation: Make the trigger fire-and-forget: drop timeout_milliseconds to ~5000 and split /api/cron into a fast ACK endpoint that enqueues and returns 202 immediately, with the batch processed by a separate self-invoked call — or accept the timeout deliberately and add a health probe that reads the last successful tick from job_logs rather than from net._http_response.

findings.title: Sentry ingests ~490 events/day, 100% of them repeats of three cron-loop conditions — two KES 1.00 test payments alone generate 24/day
findings.evidence: Sentry org ezzahcomm / project kitabuyetu (regionUrl https://de.sentry.io): total error events last 7d = 492, all since Sentry went live ~1 day ago. Event stream sample shows one "[jobs] queue STARVATION — job types not getting a turn" at every 5-minute tick (00:05, 00:10, 00:15 … 01:00), plus "[spine] orphaned payments detected" hourly and "[jobs] N stuck job(s) exhausted max_attempts" roughly every 25 min. The orphan alert's entire input is two rows: `SELECT id,amount,mpesa_receipt_number FROM payments WHERE status='completed' AND allocation_status='received' AND payment_date BETWEEN NOW()-INTERVAL '7 days' AND NOW()-INTERVAL '15 minutes'` → two KES 1.00 payments (UI3CC5BLVO, UI3CC5BOMF, both 2026-09-03). Source: lib/services/outbox.service.ts:135 logger.error inside findSpineOrphans, called hourly from lib/jobs/handlers.ts:288-290. The same condition also produced 420 staff_operational_alert email_logs rows (316 with subject "2 completed payment(s) never reached a ledger" in 2 days) even though raiseStaffAlert (lib/services/staff-alerts.ts:67-80) correctly dedups to one email per 7 days — the surplus is the retry loop in finding #1 re-sending them.
findings.impact: ~490 outbound event ingestions/day ≈ 14,700/month. Sentry's free Developer plan is 5,000 errors/month, so the quota is exhausted in ~10 days and every genuinely new error after that is dropped — Sentry stops being an alerting system within a fortnight of being switched on. Paying to hold this noise is ~$26/mo (Team, ~KES 3,400/mo).
findings.recommendation: These are conditions, not events. Rate-limit them at source: emit the starvation and orphan logger.error at most once per hour/day (the staff-alerts.ts fingerprint+claim pattern already in the codebase is the right model and can be reused for Sentry-bound logs), or add a Sentry `beforeSend` fingerprint-and-throttle for messages starting with '[jobs] queue STARVATION' and '[spine] orphaned payments'. Separately, allocate or dismiss the two KES 1.00 payments — they will only stop after they age past the 7-day window.

findings.title: mpesa_reconcile runs ~130×/day writing an audit row each time while making zero Daraja calls; 35,582 reconciliation rows for 577 lifetime provider queries
findings.evidence: lib/services/mpesa-reconciliation.service.ts:128-142 selects `mpesa_stk_requests WHERE status='pending' AND initiated_at < NOW()-5min LIMIT 50` (note: no upper age bound, so a permanently-stuck row would be re-queried forever). Live prod: `SELECT status,count(*) FROM mpesa_stk_requests GROUP BY 1` → 28 completed, 18 failed, **0 pending** — so the loop body never executes and `_stkQuery` is never called. Yet `SELECT date_trunc('day',started_at), reconciliation_type, count(*), sum(transactions_checked) FROM mpesa_reconciliations WHERE started_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '5 days' GROUP BY 1,2` shows 117-144 'stk' runs/day with transactions_checked = 0 every day. Lifetime: 35,582 rows, 35,950 tx checked, 577 mismatches (i.e. ≥577 real Daraja STK Query calls ever). job_logs: 972 completions in 7 days at 1,065 ms avg = 1,035s of function time.
findings.impact: ~130 INSERT+UPDATE pairs/day into a 35,582-row table to record 'checked 0 transactions'. No external cost today, but the table is the second-largest source of pure bookkeeping churn after job_logs, and the missing upper age bound means one wedged STK row would silently turn this into an unbounded Daraja polling loop.
findings.recommendation: Only INSERT the mpesa_reconciliations row when `stale.length > 0` (move the run-record write after the SELECT). Add an upper bound `AND initiated_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '48 hours'` to the stale query so a permanently-pending row cannot be re-queried against Safaricom indefinitely. Give mpesa_reconcile the constant dedup key treatment alongside finding #3.

findings.title: renderTemplate's inline-fallback path discards the template's own subject — all 44,967 verification emails ever sent carry the subject "Kitabu Yetu"
findings.evidence: lib/email/templates/engine.ts:151-155: the fallback branch returns `subject: vars.subject ? String(vars.subject) : 'Kitabu Yetu'` — it never reads the fallback template's own subject. lib/services/email.service.ts:23,30 only passes `fallbackTpl?.body` to renderTemplate, so DEFAULT_TEMPLATES.group_verification_link.subject ('Verify your Kitabu Yetu group', lib/email/templates/defaults.ts:30) is unreachable for any template not present in the email_templates DB table. Live prod: `SELECT subject,count(*) FROM email_logs WHERE template_key='group_verification_link' GROUP BY 1` returns exactly one row — "Kitabu Yetu", 44,967 — spanning the very first send (2026-06-04) to the latest (2026-09-05).
findings.impact: Every fallback-rendered email is subject-less in practice. Combined with finding #1 that is ~500 identical-subject, identical-recipient messages per day — the canonical pattern for a Gmail/Resend spam classification or a domain suspension, which would take out password resets and invoices with it. Given the email outage that was only resolved on 2026-09-03, the domain's sending reputation is the asset most at risk here.
findings.recommendation: Pass the whole fallback template (subject and body) into renderTemplate and use `fallbackTpl.subject` interpolated with vars in the fallback branch, falling back to 'Kitabu Yetu' only when neither exists. One-line change at email.service.ts:30 plus the signature at engine.ts:134-140.

findings.title: Premise correction: DLR polling is no longer an external-cost item — the shipped back-off cut it from 19,127 lifetime provider calls to 331, and zero in the last 24h
findings.evidence: pg_stat_statements (reset 2026-05-07, 121 days) shows two generations of the DLR write. The pre-back-off shape `INSERT INTO sms_delivery_reports (...) ON CONFLICT (provider_message_id) DO UPDATE SET status=..., queried_at=NOW()` has **19,127 calls** — one TextSMS getdlr HTTP call each. The current shape (with `poll_count = poll_count + 1`, sms.service.ts:1148-1162) has **331 calls**. Same split on the SELECT side: old query 23,947 calls, new LEFT JOIN + geometric-backoff query (sms.service.ts:1234-1263) 160 + 182 calls. Table state: `SELECT count(*), sum(poll_count), max(queried_at) FROM sms_delivery_reports` → 118 rows, 274 cumulative polls, last poll 2026-09-03 14:25 — i.e. **0 provider DLR calls in the last 24 hours**, and 72 in the last 7 days. Meanwhile sms_poll_dlr is still the single largest consumer of job time: 622 completions / 7d, 3,608 ms avg, 12,785 ms max, 2,243s total.
findings.impact: The open roadmap item to 'replace DLR polling with a webhook so sms_poll_dlr can be deleted' (docs/audits/SMS_SYSTEM_AUDIT_2026-08-20.md:490, SMS-AUDIT-v3-FINDINGS.md:244) would now save approximately zero external calls — the back-off already solved it. Spending engineering time chasing a TextSMS webhook answer is misdirected effort. The residual cost is 2,243s of function time per week spent on a sweep that makes no provider calls at all, which is worth attention but for a completely different reason.
findings.recommendation: Close the 'DLR webhook' investigation as no-longer-cost-justified and record why, so it is not reopened. Separately, investigate why sms_poll_dlr averages 3.6s per run with an empty eligible set — its two queries measure 4.7 ms and 11.8 ms mean respectively in pg_stat_statements, so the remaining ~3.5s is connection acquisition or the campaign-refresh loop, not the sweep itself.

findings.title: WhatsApp integration is entirely dead: 317 messages, 100% status='dry_run', zero real outbound calls ever made
findings.evidence: `SELECT status, direction, count(*), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM whatsapp_messages GROUP BY 1,2` returns exactly one row: dry_run / outbound / 317, from 2026-05-29 to 2026-09-03. There is no other status in the table's history. lib/services/whatsapp.service.ts exists and is wired into the notification path.
findings.impact: No external cost (that is the point — it has never made a call), but it is live machinery on the notification hot path that silently absorbs messages, and any future 'why didn't the member get notified' investigation has to rediscover this. It also means every notification routed to WhatsApp is a message a member never received, recorded as if handled.
findings.recommendation: Either configure it or remove it from the dispatch path. If it is being kept as a placeholder, make the dry_run mode loud (a startup warning, and a distinct status the notification UI surfaces) rather than a silent success.
